final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mostly reframed the same record more narrowly. That clarification is useful but not curative. It is correct that aggregate readiness, a clean rehearsal, and general governance guidance are relevant to overall launch readiness. It is also correct that they do not by themselves satisfy the specific internal policy predicate for a material weakness affecting a named customer commitment or named launch use case. On this record, the missing disclosure-or-approved-risk-acceptance link remains unresolved. That means a clean compliance finding is not supportable, and even a caveated certification position is still describing an unresolved compliance condition rather than showing it was met. The narrowed framing improves precision, but it does not convert the record into compliant or compliant_with_caveats because the caveat is itself the unsatisfied policy predicate.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named telehealth launch use case was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this limitation before launch.
The policy text treats named customer commitments or named launch use cases as material regardless of non-core or low-volume labeling.
Legal review remains open, which leaves the disclosure predicate unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for a material limitation affecting a named segment.
